rationale: Both rewrites process the document line by line and pull emphasis handling into the same applyEmphasis helper. B's control flow is tighter. A list line opens the <ul> if needed and moves on. Any other line closes the list and is passed to renderHeaderOrParagraph, so each check happens once. A runs isListItem twice per line, and its isHeader wrapper calls headerLevel only to throw the result away before the switch calls headerLevel again. A's headerLevel also has a three-value return with a '_' discard and a special case for a header line that is nothing but hashes. B's headerLevel requires the space after the hashes and returns a simple (level, ok) pair. A's comment openly admits it skips any character after the hashes. Both include clear refactoring notes, but B's code has less redundancy and states its rules more precisely.
